summary.intent: Get PRs in the caliper repo (#430, #434, #435, #438) into a mergeable state by delegating to worker subagents, and triage the failing checks on PR #434.
summary.outcome: PR #435's merge conflict with main was resolved by a subagent (signed merge commit 5b75528f, local lint/doc-check/nextest passing), leaving it BLOCKED on required checks/approval. PR #434's CI failures were diagnosed as coming from its own verify-checker-install recipe (digest-mismatch in all four Install jobs), and closing it as superseded by #438 was recommended.

repo: PR #435 shows mergeStateStatus BLOCKED after the conflict fix; it is waiting on required checks/review (Entire Gates approval), not on a conflict.

`just lint doc-check machete typos` and `cargo nextest run -p caliper-docgen-core -p caliper-docgen-semantic` are the local validation set for core/semantic changes; both had to run outside the sandbox.
`just test-checker-lane` only needs to run when construct rows or expectations are touched.
A clean git auto-merge can still fail to compile: main's new use of `diagnostics` after `drop_superseded` collided with the branch's `MergedProps { kept, unread, diagnostics }` destructuring.
Syntax diagnostics must be appended after the checker's own diagnostics in semantic_hook.rs so they are never dropped.
PR #434 ships the tsrs binary as an `@tsrs/<platform>` optionalDependency, which #438 (in-process tsrs crates) replaces; slice 4 of #369 deletes this packaging.
Worktree gotcha: a worker's local branch had to be named `fix/oxc-order-findings` because another worktree already had `feat/oxc-supplies-defaults-and-order` checked out.

code.finding: The conflict was only in the doc comment on `merge_semantic_with`. Main's `drop_superseded` replaces the old `retain` block, and `DiagnosticCode::superseded_by_checker` marks superseded structural diagnostics. Syntax diagnostics are appended after it.
The auto-merge produced a use-after-move compile error. The merge's diagnostics were renamed to `syntax` and appended after the provenance diagnostic.
The S7 item had to keep both main's note that Windows was dropped (trail 370) and this branch's S7a/S7a2 record.

workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output and not user approval; the main session summarized them without treating them as authority.
Judge subagent check results by exit code and report what was not run, such as CI polling and the checker lane.
Closing a superseded PR is left to the user; the assistant proposed the exact `gh pr close` command instead of running it.
Before repairing a failing PR, check whether the work is superseded by another PR, since a fix may be wasted effort.

friction: PR #434 has failures in four Install jobs (Node 24 and 26, npm and pnpm), the CI aggregate job, and Entire Gates, and the root cause of the digest mismatch was not found.
PR #434 became DIRTY again because main moved after the last merge.
Lint and nextest had to be run outside the sandbox.
CI status for #435 was not polled, so the final state is unverified.
open_items: User decision on closing PR #434 (recommended) or sending a worker to chase the digest mismatch and merge main.
The Callisto 0.20.0 bump worker was still running.
PRs #430, #435 and #438 are waiting on required checks and user approval (Entire Gates).
Poll CI on #435 after the merge to confirm checks pass.
Slice 4 of #369 should delete the @tsrs/<platform> packaging.
